organization.new_project_description: A project is a repository, an application or an image whose SBOM CI uploads. It comes with its own upload token, shown on its page.

project.via_title: Direct dependencies of the project leading to this component: {names}

project.badge_off: Turning the badge on publishes the number of open findings of the latest version to anyone with the badge's address, such as readers of a README. Nothing else about the project is shown.
project.badge_on: Anyone with this address sees the open findings of the latest version, after triage.
project.badge_version_hint: Add ?version=<name> to the image address to show another version.
project.token_description: CI sends this project's SBOMs with this token. It uploads to this project only, and reads it.
project.token_github_hint: Store the token as the repository secret NANOBOM_TOKEN, then add this step to a workflow, after the checkout.
project.token_curl_hint: With the token in the NANOBOM_TOKEN variable and the SBOM in sbom.json.
project.token_renew_warning: Renewing replaces the token at once: CI that still uses the old one fails until its secret is updated.
project.no_upload_text: Findings appear once CI uploads the first SBOM of this project.
project.licenses_caption: Components breaking the license policy, forbidden first

licenses_more.other: {count} more components are not listed here; the read API lists every one.

project.licenses_none: Every component's license is allowed by the organization's policy.
project.inactive_text: Runs no longer check it, and its findings are left out of counts, search and notifications. An upload to it, or a user who manages projects, makes it active again.
project.versions_description: Inactive versions are no longer checked, counted or notified, and stay readable. At most 50 versions are active: past that, an upload makes the version uploaded to the longest ago inactive.
project.versions_caption: Versions of the project, newest first, with their open findings
project.delete_version_confirm: Delete {version} with its components, upload history and findings

report.assessed_title: Assessed as not affecting the product
report.assessed_description: Findings members assessed and ignored, with their reason. A justification states why the product is not affected; an ignore without one records an accepted risk. This is the readable form of the VEX statements.
report.vex_export: For machine-readable use, the VEX export:

assessed_more.one: And {count} more, listed on the project page.
assessed_more.other: And {count} more, listed on the project page.

licenses_more.other: And {count} more components, listed on the project page.

report.licenses_no_policy: Components by license expression, as declared in the SBOM. The organization has no active license policy.
report.licenses_counts_caption: Components by license expression, most common first
report.method_checks: nanobom checks the package URL of each component of the SBOM against the OSV vulnerability database, then ranks the findings with the CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities (KEV) and the FIRST exploit prediction scores (EPSS).
report.method_limits: It does not check components without a package URL, nor code the SBOM does not list, such as vendored or generated code.
report.method_time: This report reflects the state at the time it was generated. Dates are in UTC.

finding.title: Finding
finding.reason_hint: Why this finding does not apply or is accepted; kept in the history.
finding.justification_hint: Why the product is not affected, in the CycloneDX vocabulary. VEX exports state not_affected only for ignores with a justification.
finding.justification_requires_configuration: Requires a configuration not in use
finding.ignore_until_hint: The finding opens again after this date (UTC).
finding.introduced_via_description: The direct dependencies of the project that pull in this component, per the latest SBOM. Upgrading one of them can remove it.
finding.no_dependency_graph: The latest SBOM does not say which components the project depends on directly, so the path to this component is unknown.
finding.not_linked: The dependency graph of the latest SBOM does not link this component to a direct dependency of the project.
finding.partial_graph: Some links of the dependency graph could not be followed (components without a package URL, or a reference shared by several packages), so other paths may exist.
finding.also_affected_description: In the organizations you can see.
finding.exploitation_none: No exploitation is known for this vulnerability.
finding.versions_description: Where each version stands with this vulnerability or its aliases.

settings.title: Settings
settings.members_description: Viewers read; members also ignore findings and start checks; admins also manage members, projects, tokens, the webhook, email notifications and the license policy; owners also manage owners. Roles from the identity provider's groups are shown apart and follow each sign-in.
settings.add_user_hint: Username or email address of an existing account.
settings.tokens_description: CI sends SBOMs with an upload token in the Authorization header; scripts and dashboards read through the API with a read token, which changes nothing. An organization token with the upload scope may also create projects; a project token only reaches its project. Each project also has its own upload token, shown and renewed on its page.
settings.new_token_text: Copy it now and store it as a CI secret: it will not be shown again.
settings.webhook_description: After each check, new findings at or above the chosen severity are sent to the URL, as a JSON document or as a Slack or Microsoft Teams message (described in the guide's webhook reference: https://alixanneraud.github.io/nanobom/reference/webhooks.html).
settings.email_description: After each check, new findings at or above the chosen severity, and projects that stop sending SBOMs, are emailed to these addresses in one message (described in the guide's notification reference: https://alixanneraud.github.io/nanobom/reference/webhooks.html).
settings.email_unavailable: Email is off on this server: its operator has not configured an SMTP server (NANOBOM_SMTP_URL).
settings.email_recipients: Recipients (one address per line, at most 20)
settings.delete_description: Its projects, findings, tokens and memberships are deleted for good.
settings.licenses_description: Which component licenses this organization allows, warns about or forbids. Each license of an SPDX expression gets its rule: OR takes the most permissive choice, AND the strictest. Violations show on project pages, and uploads with fail_on=license fail on forbidden licenses (see https://alixanneraud.github.io/nanobom/how-to/license-policy.html).
settings.licenses_hint: SPDX license identifiers (https://spdx.org/licenses), in any case, or LicenseRef-… names, separated by spaces, commas or new lines. Saving replaces every list.
